# Egret

> Egret is a browser game engine. Start a 2D game with `play` and `egret2d.js`. Start a 3D game with `play3d` and `egret3d.js`. Both also have module entry points.

## Choose what you need

- [Create the first 2D interaction](guide/cards/game/first-playable-world.txt) to give the player a visible target, a change in the scene and a next action. Read [action feedback](guide/cards/game/action-body-feedback.txt) for movement, landing or impact.
- [Start a 3D scene](knowledge-base/en/docs/play3d.md) with a controllable object, a camera and a goal. Load the [rolling-ball game](examples/play/roll3d.mjs) when you need a complete example.
- [Work on an existing game](guide/cards/entries/choose-entry.txt) by checking its engine version and imports. Use the [public entry points](knowledge-base/en/docs/entry-points.md) to find the features available in that build.
- Decide where the game ships before its first screen. A [web page or shared link](guide/cards/ship/ship-web-page.txt), a [phone app in a store](guide/cards/ship/ship-mobile-app.txt), a [WeChat mini game](guide/cards/ship/ship-wechat-minigame.txt) and a [Steam game](guide/cards/ship/ship-steam-desktop.txt) ask different things of input, screens, size, saves and services. A finished browser game becomes a mini game through the [WeChat export](knowledge-base/en/docs/wechat-minigame.md).
- [Investigate an error](guide/cards/errors/read-engine-errors.txt) using the exact error code, cause and what the player did. For [2D geometry limits and a black screen after a glow](guide/cards/perf/geometry-budget-2d.txt), check the action frame and the scenery already attached to the stage.

Browse the [guide index](guide/index.txt) or, in a checkout, run `node tools/egret-guide.mjs <symptom, API name or error code>`. Use `--card <id>` to read one card. Use the online entry to follow links from a standalone download <https://github.com/cnedwin/Egret_rebuild/blob/main/llms.txt>.

If the brief sets a source-size limit and you have file tools, count the final UTF-8 bytes. In a checkout, `node -p "require('node:fs').statSync('main.mjs').size"` reports the bytes for that file. Include each file covered by the limit. If over, trim secondary decoration and verify the first action again.

## Run a minimal game

```html
<!doctype html>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Light the signal</title>
<script src="egret2d.js"></script>
<script type="module">
const { play } = Egret;
let signal, label;

await play({
  width: 480, height: 270, background: 0x101828,
  setup(game) {
    signal = game.circle(240, 115, 24, 0x466074);
    label = game.text('Press Space to light the signal', { x: 240, y: 168, align: 'center' });
  },
  update(dt, game) {
    if (game.keys.pressed('space')) {
      signal.graphics.clear().beginFill(0xffce73).drawCircle(0, 0, 24).endFill();
      label.text = 'Signal lit';
    }
  }
});
</script>
```

`play` makes the canvas, fills the window with it and keeps the stage's shape. Do not add a canvas, CSS or a loop. The page opens from a folder or from a server. `egret2d.js` is beside the page: it is in a release, or `node tools/pack-single-file.mjs` makes it in a checkout. In a project with modules, `import { play } from '@egret/engine/play'` is the same function.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `x`, `y` of `game.rect` and `game.circle` is the **middle** of the shape. `y` of `game.text` is the **top** of the words.
- A colour is a number, `0xRRGGBB`. A string such as `'#ff0000'` is refused.
- `dt` is in **seconds**: move by `speed * dt`, with speed in units a second.
- Give every variable of the game its value in `setup`, not where it is declared: `game.restart()` runs `setup` again.
- Declare every variable and constant the game uses above `await play(...)`: `setup` runs before that line ends, and a `const` written below it is not there yet.
- Use `game.after`, `game.every`, `game.wait` and `game.tween`, never `setTimeout`, `setInterval` or `requestAnimationFrame`.
- When a sprite leaves the game, call `game.remove(sprite)` and take it out of your own lists. It may still be set until that update ends; after that setting it throws, and its `isDisposed` is true.
- To change how a sprite looks, draw it again: `sprite.graphics.clear().beginFill(color).drawRect(-10, -10, 20, 20).endFill()`.
- A browser plays no sound before the first key or click. That is expected; do not work around it.
- An error's message says what was wrong and ends with `Cause: …`. Read it to the end before changing anything.

## Options of `play`

`width` and `height` are the stage in the game's own units, whole numbers above 0, and are required. `background` is the colour behind everything, black unless given. `setup(game)` builds the game and may be `async`; `update(dt, game)` is one step, and is not called before `setup` has finished. `parent` is an element to put the canvas in instead of filling the window. `seed` makes `game.random` repeat. `onError(error)` is told of what stopped the game, which is otherwise thrown to the console. Translucent colours mix as in a 2D canvas: white at an alpha of 0.1 over a dark background is a faint white. `blendSpace` set to `'linear'` mixes light instead, which makes the same white look stronger.

For a phone held either way, give `fit: 'expand'` and a `portrait` size: the stage keeps its scale and reaches to the window's edges, `(0, 0)` stays the design's corner, and `width` × `height` follow the window's shape. `arrange(game)` runs after `setup` and whenever the window changes size or turns; place what belongs at an edge there, from `game.safe` (what no notch covers) or `game.screen` (all the window shows), and read `game.orientation`. Boxes of words, menus and the touch stick go in `game.safe` by themselves.

## Drawing

| Call | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `game.rect(x, y, width, height, color, layer?)` | A filled rectangle, its middle at (x, y) |
| `game.circle(x, y, radius, color, layer?)` | A filled circle, its middle at (x, y) |
| `game.sprite(g => …, layer?)` | A sprite with what the function draws around its own (0, 0) |
| `game.text(words, { x, y, size, color, align, bold, baseline, layer })` | Text: `size` 24, `color` white, `align` `'left'`, `'center'` or `'right'`, `baseline` `'top'` or `'middle'` |
| `game.button(words, { x, y, width, height, color, textColor, size, layer }, onTap)` | A button, its middle at (x, y); `button.label.text` changes its words |
| `await game.image('hero.png', { x, y, width, height, smooth, layer })` | A picture from a file beside the page, its middle at (x, y); one of `width`, `height` keeps its shape. Smooth, and kept clean when drawn small; `smooth: false` for pixel art |
| `game.remove(sprite)` | Takes it and what is in it off the stage |
| `game.toFront(sprite)` | Puts it in front of the others of its layer |

`g` draws with `beginFill(color, alpha?)`, `drawRect(x, y, w, h)`, `drawRoundRect(x, y, w, h, corner)`, `drawCircle(x, y, r)`, `drawEllipse(x, y, w, h)` (x, y is the top left of its box), `lineStyle(thickness, color, alpha?)`, `moveTo(x, y)`, `lineTo(x, y)`, `curveTo(cx, cy, x, y)`, `endFill()` and `clear()`; each returns `g`. `lineStyle()` with no thickness ends the line; a shape drawn with a line and no fill is an outline. `game.mix(a, b, t)` is the colour a fraction `t` of the way from `a` to `b`. A triangle is `g.beginFill(c).moveTo(0, -10).lineTo(8, 8).lineTo(-8, 8).endFill()`. A gradient takes stops of `{ offset, color, alpha? }`, offset 0 to 1: `g.beginLinearGradientFill(x0, y0, x1, y1, stops)` runs from one point to another and `g.beginRadialGradientFill(x, y, radius, stops)` from a centre out, as a sky or a halo; `g.lineLinearGradientStyle(x0, y0, x1, y1, stops)` and `g.lineRadialGradientStyle(x, y, radius, stops)`, after `lineStyle`, give a line the same, as a neon line.

Every one of these is a sprite. Set `x`, `y`, `rotation` (degrees, clockwise), `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `alpha` (0 to 1) and `visible`; read `width` and `height`; add properties of your own (`enemy.hp = 3`). It turns and scales about its origin. Sprites are drawn in the order they were made, later ones in front. `s.mask = other` shows `s` only where the sprite `other` draws, faded where it is translucent, and does not draw `other`: a torch's circle in the dark, with a radial gradient from white to transparent for a soft edge; `s.mask = { x, y, width, height }` clips it to a rectangle; `s.mask = null` ends it. `s.blendMode` is `'normal'`, `'add'` (light on light, for glows and neon), `'multiply'`, `'screen'` or `'erase'`; `s.renderEffect = { glow: { color, blur: 6 } }` makes it glow.

Layers: `game.world` holds what is made, and scrolls with `game.view.x` and `game.view.y`. `game.ui` is over it and stays put; text and buttons go there. Pass `game.ui` as `layer` for a bar or a panel. Pass a sprite as `layer` to make something inside it, moving, turning and fading with it. `game.text` takes `layer: 'world'` for words that scroll with the world, and `layer: sprite` for words on a sprite.

Text: `label.text = 'Score ' + n` changes it, and `label.color` and `label.size` change those. `\n` starts a new line. It is a sprite, so it can be tweened and removed.

`game.width` and `game.height` are the stage; `game.time` is the seconds of play.

## Input

| Ask | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `game.keys.down('left', 'a')` | Whether any of these keys is held |
| `game.keys.pressed('space')` | Whether it went down since the last update |
| `game.keys.released('space')` | Whether it came up since the last update |
| `game.keys.axis()` | Arrows and WASD, a gamepad's d-pad or left stick, or a stick on the glass, as `{ x, y }`, each -1 to 1, y down |
| `game.keys.look()` | A gamepad's right stick, for looking or aiming; 0 and 0 without one |
| `game.keys.down('space', 'pad:a')` | A gamepad's buttons are keys named `pad:a`, `pad:b`, `pad:x`, `pad:y`, `pad:l1`, `pad:r1`, `pad:l2`, `pad:r2`, `pad:select`, `pad:start` and `pad:up` … `pad:right` |
| `game.touchStick()` | A stick on the glass, bottom left unless `{ x, y, radius }`; it counts in `keys.axis()`. It and the buttons below appear once a finger touches the stage, or at once with `always: true`; a mouse does not use them. Make them in `setup`: a restart takes them away |
| `game.touchButton('A', { x, y, key: 'space' })` | A round button on the glass that holds that key while a finger is on it |
| `game.pointer.x`, `game.pointer.y` | Where the mouse or finger is, on the stage; it follows the mouse with no button held |
| `game.pointer.down`, `.pressed`, `.released` | Whether it is down, went down, or came up. A press on a button or on a sprite with `onTap` is theirs and is not `pressed` |
| `game.pointer.swipe` | `'left'`, `'right'`, `'up'` or `'down'` in the update after a swipe, else `undefined` |
| `game.pointer.over(sprite)` | Whether the pointer is over the sprite |
| `game.pointer.dx`, `.dy`, `.wheel` | How far the mouse moved and the wheel turned since the last update: for looking about |
| `game.pointer.lock()`, `game.pointer.unlock()`, `game.pointer.locked` | Hides the cursor and keeps the mouse to the game, for a first-person view. Call `lock` after a click; Escape gives the mouse back |
| `game.onTap(sprite, () => …)` | Calls the function when the sprite is tapped or clicked; the one in front gets it |
| `game.gestures(sprite, { hold, doubleTap, drag, swipe, pinch })` | Long press, double tap, drag (`d.dx`, `d.dy`, `d.phase`), swipe and two-finger pinch (`scale`, `rotation`) on a sprite, in game units; returns its stop. A drag or long press is no tap |
| `game.dragAndDrop()` | `.source(sprite, { data, ghost })`, `.target(sprite, { drop, accepts, hover })` and `.dragging`: a picture made by `ghost` follows the finger, and the innermost accepting target takes `data()` |

A key is `'left'`, `'right'`, `'up'`, `'down'`, `'space'`, `'enter'`, `'escape'`, `'shift'`, a letter or a digit. Make every game playable with the pointer as well as keys, so it works on a phone.

## Sound

With a game-owned mixer, pass `audio: false` to `play` or `play3d` to skip the built-in context and presets. `game.sfx.play(name)` plays an effect made in code: `jump`, `coin`, `hit`, `hurt`, `explosion`, `shoot`, `powerup`, `bounce`, `pop`, `click`, `hum`, `wind`, `win`, `lose`. `game.sfx.play('coin', { volume: 0.5, pitch: 1.2 })` changes one play; `pitch` multiplies the pitch. Any other name is refused unless defined, and defining a name again replaces it: `game.sfx.define('zap', { wave: 'saw', from: 1200, to: 200, seconds: 0.15 })`, with `wave` one of `'sine'`, `'square'`, `'saw'`, `'triangle'`, `'noise'`; a list of tones is a jingle: `game.sfx.define('chime', [{ wave: 'sine', from: 880, seconds: 0.08 }, { wave: 'sine', from: 1320, seconds: 0.3, volume: 0.4 }])`. A tone is `{ wave, from, to, seconds, volume, decay, noise }`; only `from` and `seconds` are needed. `game.sfx.loop(name, { volume, pitch, pan })` plays one again and again until `.stop()`: music made with `define`, the `hum` of an engine whose `.pitch` a game raises with its speed, the `wind`. Its `volume`, `pitch` and `pan` can be set while it plays; a pause holds it and `restart` stops it. `game.sfx.names` lists them; `game.sfx.volume` and `game.sfx.muted` act on all.

## Music

`game.music.play('battle')` writes music in code in a mood, `'calm'`, `'mystery'`, `'tense'`, `'battle'` or `'triumph'`, and loops it; one object chooses more: `game.music.play({ mood: 'battle', tempo: 150, seed: 2 })`. A new piece fades the old one out. `game.music.intensity` (0 to 1, 0.5 unless set) brings in its parts: held chords always, then a bass, drums and a tune; set it as the moment grows, and it follows over a second or so. `game.music.volume` (0.6) and `game.music.stop(seconds)`. Like sound, it is heard after the first key or click; a pause holds it and a restart stops it.

## Overlap

| Ask | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `game.overlaps(a, b)` | Whether two sprites overlap, as upright boxes |
| `game.hits(a, list)` | The first sprite of the list that overlaps `a`, or `undefined` |
| `game.hitsAll(a, list)` | Every sprite of the list that overlaps `a` |
| `game.near(a, b, distance)` | Whether their middles are within `distance`: the test for circles |
| `game.pushOut(a, b)` | How far to move `a` out of `b` by the shorter way, `{ x, y }`, or `undefined` when apart. A level of tiles is `const map = game.tiles(['#####', '#..#', '#####'], { size: 32, x, y, colors: { '#': 0x445566 }, layer })`: one sprite, `map.sprite`, in `layer` (a sprite, as one that is masked) or the world; `map.pushOut(hero)` is `{ x, y }` to add to the hero's place to leave its solid `#` tiles, or `undefined`, `map.solidAt(x, y)`, `map.at(column, row)` and `map.set(column, row, '.')` |

A sprite with `visible = false` or removed overlaps nothing; one with `alpha` 0 still does. A sprite never hits itself.

## Time and motion

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `game.after(seconds, fn)` | Calls `fn` once; returns a function that calls it off |
| `game.every(seconds, fn)` | Calls `fn` again and again; returns a function that ends it |
| `await game.wait(seconds)` | Waits, in an `async` function |
| `game.tween(sprite).to({ x: 100, alpha: 0 }, 0.3, 'quadOut')` | Moves numbers over time; starts by itself. Chain `.to`, `.wait(s)`, `.call(fn)`, `.loop(times)` (`.loop()` repeats for ever): steps run one after another. Two tweens of one property fight; `game.remove` a sprite to end its tweens |
| `await game.tween(sprite).to({ y: 200 }, 0.2).done` | Waits for it to finish |
| `game.timeScale = 0.5` | Slow motion |
| `game.pause()`, `game.resume()`, `game.paused` | Stops and starts updates, timers and tweens; `update` is not called while paused, so keys are not asked, but a button still works |
| `game.restart()` | Clears the world, the ui, timers and tweens, and runs `setup` again |

Easings: `linear`, `quadIn`, `quadOut`, `quadInOut`, `cubicOut`, `backOut`, `elasticOut`, `bounceOut`.

## Feel

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `game.shake(amount = 6, seconds = 0.25)` | Shakes the world; the ui stays put |
| `game.flash(color = 0xffffff, seconds = 0.15)` | A colour over the stage that fades. With `game.reducedMotion` (follows `prefers-reduced-motion`, settable) flashes are faint and shakes do nothing |
| `game.hitStop(seconds = 0.06)` | Freezes play for a moment |
| `game.burst(x, y, { color, count, speed, life, size, gravity })` | Throws pieces out from a point of the world |

Use them: a hit wants a sound, a burst and a small shake; a death wants a flash.

## Words, menus and bars

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `game.bar({ x, y, width, height, value, max, color, back, layer })` | A bar of health, time or power, on the ui unless `layer`; `x`, `y` is its top left. Set `bar.value` and it slides there; a fall leaves a pale trail |
| `game.toast('Saved')` | A short notice at the top that fades after 2 seconds, or `{ seconds }`; several stack |
| `await game.say('words', { who, choices, color, speed })` | A box of words at the bottom, shown letter by letter and wrapped; words longer than a box holds (about three lines) go on in a second box. It does not pause the game: check `game.asking`. Space, Enter, Z or a tap shows the rest, another closes it. With `choices` it gives the index chosen with the arrows and Enter or a tap; without, undefined |
| `await game.menu(['Start', 'Quit'], { title })` | A list in the middle of the stage; gives the index chosen |
| `game.asking` | Whether a box of words or a menu is open; an `update` can return early while it is |

`setup` may await them: frames are drawn while it waits, so a title menu or a first line of a story is `await game.menu(...)` in `setup`. They answer while the game is paused. Boxes asked for while one is open wait their turn. A restart takes them away.

## Chance and saves

`game.random.int(1, 6)`, `.range(0, 1)`, `.chance(0.25)`, `.pick(list)` and `.shuffle(list)`, which gives a new list. `game.save('best', score)` keeps a value between visits and `game.load('best', 0)` reads it, or gives the second argument.

## Complete games

- [Breakout](examples/play/breakout.mjs) for a short arcade loop with lives and restart.
- [Platformer](examples/play/platformer.mjs) for motion, ground collision and a scrolling level.
- [Memory](examples/play/memory.mjs) for turns, matching and a saved best score.
- [Rolling Ball](examples/play/roll3d.mjs) for a 3D camera, movement and collection.
- [Run the examples](examples/play/README.md) to open these games with the checkout server.

## 3D

`play3d` is `play` with a world of three dimensions under it. The page loads `egret3d.js` instead of `egret2d.js`, and the script starts with `const { play3d } = Egret;`. Everything above is the same and is the flat interface over the picture, in the units of `width` and `height`: `game.text`, `game.button`, `game.keys`, `game.pointer`, `game.sfx`, `game.tween`, `game.after`, `game.flash`, `game.restart`. What is added is the world. `x` is right, `y` is up, `z` is towards the camera; a ball of radius 0.5 on a ground of 24 reads well.

| Call | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `game.box(width, height, depth, color, { x, y, z })` | A box, its middle at the place |
| `game.sphere(radius, color, { x, y, z })`, `game.cylinder(radius, height, color, { x, y, z })`, `game.cone(radius, height, color, { x, y, z })` | A ball; a cylinder on its end; a cone on its base |
| `game.ground(size, color, y = 0)` | A square floor whose top is at height `y` |
| `game.add(model, { x, y, z })` | Makes a model of your own a thing: a `Mesh3D` of your geometry, a group, or a loaded glTF. Its box is worked out from its geometry; it keeps its colours |
| `game.remove(thing)` | Takes it out of the world; `thing.removed` is then true, and setting it does nothing |
| `game.group([a, b, c], { x, y, z })`; `game.lamp(color, { x, y, z }, { intensity: 4, range: 8 })` | Makes things one thing, moved, turned and tested as one, their places now from the group's (test the group, not its parts); a lamp whose light fades out by its range, with `x`, `y`, `z`, `color`, `intensity` to set, put out by `game.remove(lamp)` |
| `game.onTap(thing, () => …)` | Calls the function when the thing is tapped or clicked: the nearest one under the pointer |
| `game.follow(thing, { x: 0, y: 4, z: 8, smooth: 6, turn, lookY })` | Keeps the camera that far from a thing, looking at it, or `lookY` above it to frame a tower or the sky; `turn: true` keeps it behind as the thing's `rotationY` turns. `game.camera.fov` is the angle it sees from top to bottom, in degrees: more for a wide view |
| `game.overlaps(a, b)`, `game.hits(a, list)`, `game.hitsAll(a, list)` | Overlap of things as upright boxes |
| `game.near(a, b, distance?)` | Whether their middles are within a distance, the sum of their radii unless given |
| `game.pushOut(a, b)` | How far to move `a` out of `b`: `{ x, y, z }`, one of them not 0, or `undefined`. A `y` above 0 means `a` stands on `b` |
| `game.shake(amount = 0.3, seconds = 0.25)` | Shakes the camera, in units of the world |
| `game.burst(x, y, z, { color, count, speed, life, size, gravity })` | Throws small pieces out from a point |

A thing has `x`, `y`, `z`, `rotationX`, `rotationY`, `rotationZ` (degrees), `scale`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `scaleZ`, `visible`, `color`, `glow` (0 unless set; 1 or more makes it shine with its colour, as a lantern at night, and through fog) and `opacity` (1 unless set; less lets what is behind show through, as glass, and with `glow` a beam of light), all of which can be set and tweened, and takes properties of your own. Every shape is placed by its middle. `rotationY` turns a thing to its left, counterclockwise seen from above; at 0 it faces away from the camera, towards -z, so forward is `x -= Math.sin(r) * d; z -= Math.cos(r) * d` with `r = thing.rotationY * Math.PI / 180`, and a turned child of a group turns with it. A cylinder or a cone stands upright; `rotationZ = 90` lays it on its side, along x, and `rotationX = 90` along z, as a beam from a lamp. Without `follow`, set `game.camera.x`, `.y`, `.z` and call `game.camera.lookAt(x, y, z)`. `game.sun` lights the world and every thing casts and takes shadows: nothing to set. Shadows are drawn at the quality the device gets (`medium` or `high`); a software-rendered browser gets `low`, without them, and `game.app.setQuality('medium')` asks for them anyway. A turned thing is still tested as an upright box of its unturned size; `game.scene` and `game.app` are the World3D scene and app under it. There is no gravity: move things yourself, and use `pushOut` to stand them on one another.

`game.look('dusk')` sets the light and air of the world: `'day'` (as it starts), `'dusk'`, `'night'`, `'fog'` or `'snow'`, or `{ background, sky, ground, light, sun, sunIntensity, sunFrom, fog }` to change parts of one, the rest staying, as often as every frame. `background`, `sky` (the light from above), `ground` (from below) and `sun` are colours; `light` and `sunIntensity` are strengths, 0 to 16 (night 0.22 and 0.35, day 0.9 and 2.4); `sunFrom` is `[x, y, z]`; `fog` is its thickness, 0 clear, 0.02 a haze, 0.06 a fog. A thing that glows is seen through fog and snow. `game.weather('snow')`, `'rain'` or `'none'`, with `{ amount }` 1 unless given, lets snow or rain fall around what the camera looks at.


## Check a game

In a checkout, `node tools/verify-game.mjs <absolute Playwright index.mjs> <game.html> <new output directory> [play.mjs]` runs the page in a headless browser, plays it blind with keys, clicks and drags, and reports whether it started without an error, drew, kept running, changed under input and made a sound. Run it after writing or changing a game, and read the three pictures it saves. For a 3D model made in code, `node tools/model-preview.mjs <absolute Playwright index.mjs> <model.mjs> <picture.png>` draws it from four sides; look at it after each change.

Blind play does not reach a win or a loss. The optional `play.mjs` plays the game as a person would, in the stage's own units, and reads the page by the colour at a place. It starts a new game, with what blind play saved forgotten. `player.until(test, label, seconds)` looks about every 0.12 seconds of real time until `test(look)` is true and fails after `seconds`, 20 unless given; `player.wait(seconds)` waits. What a game keeps on `window` (`window.state = state`) is read with `player.read(() => window.state.collected)`, so a script need not time its moves:

```js
export const stage = { width: 480, height: 270 };
export default async function (player) {
  await player.hold('right');                         // player.key('space') presses; player.tap(x, y) taps; player.drag(x0, y0, x1, y1) drags
  await player.until(look => player.alike(look(170, 150), 0x3b82f6), 'the button of the win screen', 30);
  await player.letGo('right');
  await player.picture('won');
}
```

## Beyond this page

`game.browser`, `game.engine` and `game.scope` are the engine under `play`; what the other entries make can be added to `game.world` and `game.ui`.

- [Play, in full](knowledge-base/en/docs/play.md): every option, sound recipes, what is checked
- [Graphics](knowledge-base/en/docs/graphics.md): gradients, dashes, arcs, image fills
- [The browser game](knowledge-base/en/docs/browser-game.md): images, labels and the loop without `play`
- [Audio](knowledge-base/en/docs/audio.md): music and sound files
- [The game kit](knowledge-base/en/docs/game-kit.md): input by action, gamepads, touch controls, larger saves
- [2D camera](knowledge-base/en/docs/camera-2d.md), [tile maps](knowledge-base/en/docs/tilemap.md), [particles](knowledge-base/en/docs/particles.md), [2D physics](knowledge-base/en/docs/physics-2d.md), [interface controls](knowledge-base/en/docs/ui-controls.md)
- [Play3D, in full](knowledge-base/en/docs/play3d.md), and [World3D](knowledge-base/en/docs/world3d-app.md) under it: models, materials, lights, physics
- [Error codes](knowledge-base/en/docs/error-codes.md) and [every entry](knowledge-base/en/docs/entry-points.md)

For a larger game, ask the [guide](guide/index.txt) instead of reading more pages: it holds small cards, each learnt from games built on the engine. In a checkout, `node tools/egret-guide.mjs <words, an engine name, an error code or a devtools hint id>` prints the two or three cards that answer, and `--card <id>` prints one.
